output.headline: A sponsor with an open platform in the sub-sector, a 2024 same-sub-sector deal and a record of paying upper-quartile multiples; the target fits as an add-on.
output.differentiator: An open platform in the sub-sector gives it an add-on route, and its median 15.5x paid sits above the comparable 75th percentile of 15.3x. Peer comparison not shown here.
output.why_them: Add-on to an open platform; pays upper-quartile multiples

acquirer_overview.title: Global sponsor with an 18-deal healthcare record since 2016
points: Financial sponsor with 18 deals between 2016 and 2024; 15 of 18 (83%) closed, and 17 of 18 (94%) were control deals. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share]
Flagship fund Advent Global Private Equity X is about $25 billion (2022 vintage); AUM approximately $100 billion as of November 2025. [P:1, P:2]
Median deal is $124M, and 8 of 18 deals fall in the comparable $100M-$400M size band; 5 deals since 2022. [T:record, K:size_band, K:recent]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: An add-on to an open platform, backed by provider deals
points: Deals in this or neighbouring sub-sectors are a modest factor in its likelihood; it has 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and 7 in adjacent provider sub-sectors. [S:sector_rel, T:record]
Its open platform in the sub-sector makes the target an add-on rather than a new bet, and the size fits. [A:angles]
Margin Improvement drove 7 of 18 of its deals, which suits a target with a 16.8% EBITDA margin. [M:margin_improvement, X:target]

precedent_activity.title: Recent own-sub-sector and behavioral health deals at 9.3x to 14.6x
points: Crest Care Partners, 2024: $304M recapitalization in the target's own sub-sector at 9.3x EV/EBITDA; closed. [D:MA-2024-0120]
Crown Addiction Treatment, 2023: $123M recapitalization at 14.6x, an adjacent provider sub-sector (behavioral health); closed. [D:MA-2023-0108]
Summit DSO, 2018: $303M merger of equals in the Midwest at 11.7x; closed. [D:MA-2018-0184]

valuation_context.title: The 75th percentile is defensible, and its own pricing supports it
points: 70 comparable deals price at 10.7x (25th percentile), 12.8x (median) and 15.3x (75th percentile) EV/EBITDA. [V:comps]
The target's 16.8% margin is above the comps' median of 12.9% and above 87% of comps, which supports the 75th percentile. [V:comps]
Its median multiple paid is 15.5x. At 5.0x leverage, maximum price is $193M at a same-sector exit and $216M at a 15.0x platform exit. [V:comps, V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below its 20% target. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.reality: The bid works only if it underwrites the add-on exit; the same-exit maximum is $193M. [V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Limited Midwest footprint
risk_flags.concern: Prior purchases in this or a neighbouring region are a slight factor against; it has 1 deal in the target's region. [S:geo_fit, T:record]
risk_flags.mitigant: That deal, Summit DSO ($303M, 2018), was in the Midwest and closed. [D:MA-2018-0184]
risk_flags.reality: Region is a minor negative, and sub-sector and platform fit carry the case. [S:geo_fit, S:sector_rel]

risk_flags.title: Thin own-sub-sector record
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 of 18 deals is in the target's own sub-sector, and 10 are outside provider services. [T:record]
risk_flags.mitigant: 7 adjacent provider deals and an open platform in the sub-sector offer a route in. [T:record, A:angles]
risk_flags.reality: Provider deals total 8 of 18, so the fit is real but not concentrated. [A:angles]

conviction.rationale: Basis: 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and 7 in adjacent provider sub-sectors, plus an open platform in the sub-sector offering an add-on route. [C:conviction, T:record, A:angles]
